Sivan Spices — Goal & Vision

Authentic flavor, built like a technology product

A working overview of where Sivan Spices is headed, why the market needs it, and the three initiatives behind it — Direct to Customer, Wholesale & Operations, and Expansion.

Vision

Sivan Spices brings authentic, small-batch Indian flavors to American kitchens. It's built and run as a modern, AI-native food business from day one. Customer experience, internal operations, and business expansion are all powered by the same technology discipline used to build world-class software products.

The goal is to grow from a single-founder spice brand into a scalable food business. That means expanding retail partnerships and deepening customer relationships through intelligent digital tools.

Market opportunity & gap

The US market for Indian spices is large, but genuinely authentic options are rare. Most widely available spice mixes are mass-produced for shelf life, scale, and cost — not flavor — which has quietly reset what "normal" tastes like for most customers.

The gap isn't a lack of demand — it's a lack of authenticity in supply. When customers actually taste spices made the way they're meant to be made, the reaction is recognition: they remember what they'd been missing, often without realizing they'd been missing anything at all.

$7.2B US seasonings & spices market (2025 est.)
5.2M Indian-Americans in the US — fastest-growing major Asian-American group
~$170M Conservative addressable spend on spice mixes specifically, within that population

Methodology: ~1.3M Indian-American households (5.2M ÷ 4) × ~65% purchasing packaged spice mixes × ~$200/yr ($75–300 depending on cooking frequency; blended estimate based on observed customer purchasing patterns).

Go-to-market

The spice aisle is crowded — most shoppers already have a brand they default to, whether or not it's authentic. Sivan Spices isn't trying to win that space with a big launch; the approach is persistence: staying visible, building real relationships store by store, and letting steady, repeatable growth compound over time rather than chasing a fast breakout.

Two channels, in order: direct-to-consumer — online at sivanspices.com and in-person at retail stores — and wholesale, to reach a wider footprint of retail stores without building a sales team.

The table below is a conservative starting universe for wholesale outreach — real counts, not projections, and almost certainly an undercount for the Bay Area specifically, where several cities' stores weren't individually tallied.

$50–100K Target revenue, Year 1
2,243 Indian grocery stores, USA
453 Indian grocery stores, California
88 in SF + San Jose alone — Bay Area total is higher

Store counts compiled via manual online search (Google Maps and business listings), not a licensed database — a conservative starting point, not a precise census.

Beyond dedicated Indian grocery stores, mainstream chains (Safeway, Whole Foods, Trader Joe's, and others) are increasingly stocking international/ethnic aisles as Indian and Asian flavors move into the mainstream — a longer-term expansion channel once the dedicated-store base is established.

Three initiatives

Consistent with a deliberate, slow-expansion strategy — prioritizing store relationships and repeat customers over rapid scaling.

Online Storefront for US-Wide Shipping Direct to Customer

A Shopify storefront enabling online ordering with shipping across the United States, with two AI tools built in: a Recipe Bot that helps customers discover how to use each product through personalized recipe suggestions, and an FAQ Bot that answers customer questions instantly and stays current on product availability. Built using Shopify's native AI tooling combined with Claude Code — moving from concept to live storefront features without a dedicated engineering team.

Internal operations tool Wholesale & Operations

A custom-built internal dashboard tracking invoicing, payments, sales across channels, store partnerships, and lead follow-up for retail expansion — replacing expensive, one-size-fits-all SaaS tools that don't fit an early-stage food business.

Sivan Cooks — AI-powered cook marketplace Expansion

A marketplace connecting home cooks with clients. Every entry point offers a real two-way AI voice agent — not just voice-to-text, but a live back-and-forth conversation that asks follow-up questions and fills out the signup or job posting as you talk, in English, Hindi, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, or Malayalam. Clients and cooks can also fill a form or describe their request in one voice note instead, whichever is easiest. Extends the same operational foundation into a new customer base beyond the spice brand.
